full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order being No.43 dated 11-5-99 passed by Mr AM Shahidur Rahman, Special Tribunal No.1, Satkhira in Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 1996 arising out of Satkhira Police Station Case No.16 dated 11-4-96 corresponding to OR Case No. 140/96 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. In the writ petition it has been stated, inter alia, that on 9-4-96 four Bangladeshi citizens namely, Shamsuddin, Shamol, Shamim and Motiul Alam came from India with some goods under Baggage Rules and they after completing immigration checking from immigration checking post produced the goods to the Customs House, Jessore for assessing Customs Duty. VAT and other taxes. But their goods were not released and those were temporarily held up due to the arrival of some higher customs officers from Khulna and those passengers were given receipts against their goods. On 10-4-96 at 5-30 PM the present petitioners namely, Sirajul Islam and Md Aminul Islam came from India with Indian goods under Baggage Rules and they kept their goods in a room of Immigration checkpost of Vomra with their legal passports and when they met with the aforesaid 4(four) businessmen who came from India on 9-4-96. They were informed by them that their (the said four persons) goods had not been released till then as in the meantime BDR personnel came to the spot and seized the aforesaid goods on the basis of false and baseless information. Thereafter on 10-4-96 Naik Md Golam Nabi of 21 Rifles Battalion, Satkhira lodged a first information report with Satkhira Police Station against the petitioners and the said 4(four) persons under section 25(B) of the Special Powers Act 1974 and the said First Information Report gave rise to Satkhira Police Station case No.16 dated 10-4-96 corresponding to OR No. 140/96. The Police after investigation submitted final report being No.80 dated 16-7-96 under section 26(B) of the Special Powers Act 1974 stating that the accused persons brought the seized sarees lawfully from India and the First Information Report was lodged upon wrong information. The learned Magistrate 1st Class Nalishi Adaltat Zone 'Kha' Satkhira after receiving the final report by his order dated 1-8-96 sent the case record to the Special Tribunal No.1, Satkhira who took cognizance in the case by this order dated 18-11-96 on the basis of a Naraji Petition filed by the Informant and the case was registered as Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 96. Against the acceptance of Naraji Petition accused persons namely, Md Shamsuddin Ahmed alias Alauddin, Shyamal Mallick and Md Matiul Alam filed Criminal Miscellaneous case No.3231 of 1997 before this court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the said Special Tribunal Case. Eventually, a Division Bench of this Court by Judgment and Order dated 27-11-1997 made the Rule absolute in the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case and the proceeding of Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 1996 of the Court of Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira was quashed. After the disposal of the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case Matiul Alam Bhuiyan, Shamal Mittra, Shamim and Shamsuddin who were accused in the said Special Tribunal case filed a petition before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira to release the goods seized by the customs authority in their favour and the learned Special Tribunal by order No.37 dated 3-3-99 directed the Customs authority to return the goods to the claimants as per their individual statement after realising VAT as per law. After the passing of the said order the petitioners filed an application before the learned Special Tribunal Satkhira to stay the operation of said order No.37 dated 3-3-99 till the ascertainment of ownership of the seized goods and the Special Tribunal by his order No.38 dated 16-3-99 directed the customs authority to take necessary order from the tribunal for releasing the goods after submission of the list of the seized goods by them. Thereafter, the present petitioners filed another application before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira for releasing the seized goods in their favour as per the final report submitted by the investigating officer and the Special Tribunal by his order No.42 dated 6-5-99 rejected the petition of the petitioners and maintained the order dated 3-3-99. The petitioners filed a review petition before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira for re-considering the order dated 6-5-99 and the Special Tribunal by his order No.43 dated 11-5-99 maintained the earlier order passed on 3-3-99 and directed the customs authority to return the seized goods to all the 6(six) first information report named accused persons on strict scrutiny of the individual claims. Thereafter the petitioners filed an application before the Special Tribunal Satkhira for staying the operation of order Nos.37 and 43 dated 3-3-99 and dated 11-5-99 respectively who by order No. 44 dated 27-5-99 stayed the operation of the aforesaid orders up to 30-6-99. The petitioners applied for the certified copy of the order dared 11-5-99 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 1 Satkhira in the said Special Tribunal Case and obtained the same on 23-6-99. The petitioner No.1 is the tadbirker of the case and had come to Dhaka on 30-6-99 for consultation with his learned Advocate Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury and after consultation he went home for managing costs for preferring his case against the impugned order but as ill luck would have it, the petitioner No.1 suddenly fell ill being attacked with Jaundice and under the advice of a doctor had to remain bed ridden up to 20-7-99. The petitioner No.2 was away from home and, as such, none of the petitioners could come to Dhaka to contact with their learned Advocate for preferring appeal and by this time the statutory period of 30 days for preferring appeal expired. Under the above circumstances the petitioners filed the instant writ petition arid obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the Special Tribunal acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order giving direction to return the seized goods to all the 6 accused persons as mentioned in the First Information Report and in the seizure list inasmuch as he did not at all consider the fact disclosed in the final report submitted by the police to the effect that the petitioners are the owners of the seized goods and they are entitled to get back the same and that the other accused persons never challenged the said fact mentioned in the final report and the recommendation made by the Investigating Officer. Learned Advocate further submits that in the Judgment passed by. this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3231of 1997 filed by other accused persons there being no observation or direction to return the seized goods to them, the Special Tribunal acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order maintaining the order dated 3-3- 99 which was passed to return the seized goods to all the accused persons giving reference to the Judgment passed in the said Criminal Miscellaneous case and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 5. Mr Oziullah, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 4-7, on the other hand, submits that the Special Tribunal on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as disclosed in the first information report, seizure list as well as the final report came to the definite finding that the goods were seized from all the 6(six) persons and all of them are entitled to get back the goods which are purely questions of fact and this court in exercising the jurisdiction of judicial review cannot interfere with the said finding of fact unless it can be shown that the tribunal acted without jurisdiction or acted in excess of its jurisdiction. He further submits that in the instant case the tribunal having passed the impugned order with jurisdiction and on consideration of the materials on record there is no scope to interfere with the same by this court. Mr Oziullah lastly submits that the petitioners had an alternative remedy by way of filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act and they having not availed the same writ petition itself is not maintainable in law. 

 7. After the passing of the said order, the present petitioners filed another application praying for giving them the seized goods in the light of the facts disclosed in the final report and the said application was fixed for hearing on 20-4-99 after giving notice to the State. In the meantime Superintendent of Customs, Excise and VAT Circle, Satkhira submitted the list of the claimants of the seized goods as has been noted in the order dated 22-3-99 passed by the Tribunal which was kept with the record to be put up on the date fixed. Then on the date fixed, that is on 20-4-99, the presiding Judge being on leave and the Judge-in-charge being engaged with the hearing of other cases, next date was fixed on 6-5-99. The tribunal by his order dated 6-5-99 maintained the order dated 3-3-99 as has already been mentioned hereinabove. On perusal of the impugned order, it appears that the special tribunal passed the same after hearing the parties and considering the allegations made in the First Information Report and the seizure list which is as under; 

 8. The tribunal also gave direction to the customs authority to return the goods on strict scrutiny of the individual claims as well as other evidence on the record. This court exercising the Jurisdiction of judicial review can not sit over the finding of the tribunal as a court of appeal and consequently can not interfere with the said finding of fact which is based on the materials on record. However, we have ourselves also perused the First Information Report where it has been clearly alleged that the goods were seized from all the accused persons and the seizure list was prepared accordingly. In view of the fact that the tribunal has directed the customs authority to return the goods on strict scrutiny of the individual claims as well as other evidence on record, the petitioners will have enough scope to prove their ownership in respect of the seized goods and if they can succeed that the goods were seized from their possession only, in that case they would get back the goods and, as such, we do not see any reason for the petitioners to be aggrieved by the impugned order passed by the tribunal. The basis of the petitioners claim that the goods were seized from their possession only as it appears from the writ petition is the so-called recommendation of the Investigation Officer to the effect that the goods may be released in favour of Aminul Islam and Serajul Islam (petitioners) after realising customs duty and VAT as per Baggage Rules. On scrutiny of the Final Report it appeared to us that the Investigation Officer in a vague way made the said recommendation without specifying with reference to the documents out of 100 seized items of goods, how many items were brought by them and furthermore, in law the Investigating Officer had no legal authority to make any such recommendation and, as such, the petitioners can not claim to get back the goods on such recommendation. In view of the discussion made above, we are of the view that the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira passed the impugned order legally and with jurisdiction and we do not find any substance in the submissions made by Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury. 

 9. Now, let us see whether the writ petition is maintainable or not. It appears that the impugned order was passed at the instance of the petitioners and in their presence. The order was passed by the Special Tribunal and under section 30 of the Special Powers Act an appeal lies to this court to be filed within 30 days but the petitioners did not file the appeal, instead moved this court in its writ jurisdiction. In paragraph 14 of the writ petition the petitioners have tried to explain the reasons for not preferring the statutory appeal but our considered view is that the explanations are not at all cogent and reasonable and those cannot be accepted to avoid the availability of the alternative remedy. In the case of Nesar Ahmed also known as Babul vs Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali reported in 49 DLR (AD) 1111, it has been held: 

 "10. But the presence of an alternative remedy does not debar the exercise of jurisdiction by the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution when the facts ,and circumstances of a particular case are such that the accused person had no reasonable opportunity to avail of the statutory remedy under section 30 of the Special Powers Act. whether or not the accused person had such a reasonable opportunity is a question of fact to be decided in each case upon case records and, no hard and fast formula can be laid down to settle the criteria in advance." 

 In the instant case we have seen that the impugned order was passed at the instance of the petitioners and in their presence and, as such, they had full opportunity to avail of the statutory remedy by way of filing an appeal to this court under section 30 of the Special Powers Act and, as such, we are of the view that the writ petition is also not maintainable in law, and the Rule is liable to be discharged on that count also.
